messages:
kevin-cs: Escalation from Acme: they see intermittent streaming failures that surface as 'broken pipe' in client logs and are getting billed because our gateway labels them as 5xx. Customer says it only happens during longer streaming responses (20-40s). Sample request IDs: rg_20250318_01, rg_20250318_42. Paste of client stacktrace and a small curl repro below. Can SRE triage?

maria-support: On it. Do we have gateway logs for those request IDs? Also: are they using chunked transfer-encoding or HTTP/2 streaming?

kevin-cs: They say chunked encoding over HTTP/1.1 via a node proxy. They included a short repro curl: ```curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream -d '{"prompt":"long chat..."}'``` Customer logs show `write EPIPE` and `socket hang up` on their proxy side.

sam-sre: Quick notes from looking at rg_20250318_01 in the gateway: upstream sent a final chunk, then we observed a FIN from client mid-stream (client FIN arrived before we finished flushing to client). Our current classification path marks upstream response as truncated -> increments 5xx counter if no final 200/2xx seen. That will incorrectly bill when the client terminated the TCP connection.

maria-support: So basically we think it's a client disconnect being labeled as a gateway 5xx. Customer wants a refund for those tokens. How frequent is this?

sam-sre: Based on a quick query over last 72h for that client: ~120 events tagged as `stream_truncated` for their org, 35% correlate with upstream returning 5xx, 65% are client-initiated disconnects (RST/FIN seen in conn logs). We should separate those buckets.

olivia-eng: Agreed — the classification needs to be more precise. Proposed rule: if we see client FIN/RST before any upstream 5xx status line and we didn't generate a server-side 5xx body, mark as `client_abort` and exclude from billable 5xx. Edge case: intermediaries/proxies can close before full response — still a client abort. Also need to watch for half-closed sockets where upstream is still sending but kernel ACKs are backpressure.

kevin-cs: Customer also provided a node fetch snippet that reproduces it behind their proxy: ```const res = await fetch(apiUrl, { method: 'POST', body: stream }); // later: stream.destroy(new Error('test abort'))``` They trigger stream.destroy after N seconds. They expect us to not classify this as a server 5xx.

sam-sre: Repro steps for us: 1) Start a simple server that streams chunked responses slowly (e.g., 200ms/chunk). 2) Run a client that connects then closes the socket mid-stream. 3) Confirm gateway logs show `client_fin` and our current metric increments `5xx_stream_trunc`. I can run this in staging.

maria-support: Can you capture the exact gateway log lines we should use in the billing dispute? The customer audit team wants a clear reason for the credit.

sam-sre: Will attach logs. Example gateway excerpt: ```[gateway] req=rg_20250318_01 status=INCOMPLETE reason=client_fin upstream_status= - bytes_sent=1234``` Also we have conn-level events: `tcp_event{type=FIN, src=client}`. Use those two as evidence.

olivia-eng: Quick mitigation we can deploy as a hotfix: change billing classifier to consult conn-level events before incrementing 5xx for stream truncation. Implementation: in stream proxy pipeline, when we transition to truncated state, check `conn_events` for `FIN|RST` within the request window. If present, set labeling to `client_abort` and emit a non-billable metric. I'll open a PR with tests.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline:staging starting for refactor/stream-trunc-classifier. (canary: 10% staging hosts) :rocket:

kevin-cs: Customer will accept a partial credit if we can show a plan + timeline. Can we give ETA?

sam-sre: If PR lands today, we can canary in staging tonight and target prod canary tomorrow morning. For immediate relief we can manually filter their org from the billing report (one-off credit) while we ship the classifier fix.

maria-support: I'll draft the credit note and attach the staging logs you mentioned. Also confirm whether this affects other customers — we should run a backfill to find misclassified events.

olivia-eng: I'll add a backfill job to reclassify last 30 days of `stream_truncated` events and produce a CSV of affected orgs. Note: backfill will be best-effort and might undercount if conn events weren't logged historically.

sam-sre: One more thing: watch chunked trailers. If a proxy strips trailers or injects them, we might mis-detect end-of-stream. Add an integration test that runs with chunk trailer mutated by an upstream proxy to ensure we don't flip classification erroneously.

kevin-cs: Thanks all — customer wants weekly updates until credit is resolved. I'll own comms. Please post the staging link once ops-bot finishes canary.

maria-support: Filing support-ticket S-20250318-ACME and linking this thread. Tagging @sam-sre for the logs and @olivia-eng for PR. :thumbsup:
